Model-averaged benchmark dose

Source: R/bmdma.R
bmdma.Rd

Benchmark doses (see bmd) averaged over several dose-response models fitted to the same data, with AIC or BIC weights, and bootstrap confidence intervals: the BMDL is the lower limit of the two-sided 90% interval, confint(bmdma(...)).

Usage

bmdma(
  ...,
  bmr = 0.1,
  def = c("excess", "additional", "relative", "sd"),
  newdata = NULL,
  scale = c("marginal", "conditional"),
  average = c("curve", "bmd"),
  weights = c("AIC", "BIC"),
  nodes = NULL,
  nsim = 500,
  seed = NULL,
  progress = interactive()
)

# S3 method for class 'bmdma'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmdma'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bmdma'
confint(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.9, method = c("boot", "buckland"), ...)

Arguments

...

drmTMB objects, fitted to the same response, doses and weights; the models and families may differ (e.g. gaussian and lognormal, whose AICs are comparable). Models are labelled by their argument names (e.g. LL = fit1) or, if unnamed, by the expressions. The fits are maximum likelihood fits without priors; for fits with priors, see bmdbayes.

bmr, def, newdata, scale, nodes

the benchmark response and the definition, the covariates of the curves, and the BMD of the marginal or conditional curve with random effects, as in bmd; newdata cannot give fitted groups of random effects, and def="sd" with average="curve" needs gaussian families

average

"curve" (default) for the BMD of the model-averaged curve, the weighted mean of the curves of the models, or "bmd" for the weighted mean of the BMDs of the models

weights

the information criterion of the model weights, "AIC" (default) or "BIC"

nsim

number of bootstrap samples; 0 for no bootstrap (then there is no BMDL for average="curve")

seed

an optional seed for the random number generator

progress

logical, show a progress bar

x, object

a bmdma object

digits

number of significant digits in the printed output

parm

BMDs, names or positions in coef; default all

level

the confidence level; 0.90 by default, for the BMDL and BMDU

method

"boot" for bootstrap percentile intervals, or "buckland" for Wald intervals with the standard error of Buckland et al. (1997), for average="bmd" only; by default "boot" if the bootstrap was run (nsim > 0), and "buckland" otherwise

Value

bmdma returns a bmdma object, a list with the averaged BMDs (estimates), the table of the models (models: model, family, logLik, df, AIC or BIC, weight), the bmd results of the models (bmds), the averaged BMDs of the bootstrap samples (boot, with NA rows for samples left out), their weights (bootweights, NA for failed fits) and the models the samples were simulated from (source), and the arguments. coef returns the averaged BMDs and confint their confidence intervals.

Details

AIC weights were recommended by EFSA (2017); the current guidance of EFSA (2022) uses Bayesian model averaging, see bmdbayes and bmdefsa.

Model k gets the weight exp(-IC_k/2), relative to the sum over the models, with the information criterion IC_k, AIC_k = -2 logLik_k + 2 df_k or BIC_k = -2 logLik_k + log(n) df_k, with the number of observations n (nobs), as in Ritz, Gerhard and Hothorn (2013). With average="curve", the BMD is that of the averaged curve, the weighted mean of the curves (the marginal mean curves with scale="marginal" and random effects), with the benchmark response relative to the averaged response at dose zero, as in EFSA (2017); with def="sd", the standard deviation is the weighted mean of the residual standard deviations. With average="bmd", it is the weighted mean of the BMDs of the models; models whose curve does not reach the benchmark response are left out, with the weights of the others rescaled.

The bootstrap samples the responses from the mixture of the models: for each sample, a model is drawn with its weight and a response simulated from it, with new random effects (see simulate.drmTMB). All models are fitted to each sample, starting at their estimates, and the weights and the averaged BMD are computed again. Models whose fit fails are left out of a sample, with the weights of the others rescaled; samples without any fit are left out. Models of the lognormal family get the weight 0 in samples with non-positive responses (e.g. simulated from a gaussian model), whose likelihood is zero under the lognormal family. The confidence intervals are percentile intervals of the averaged BMDs.

References

Buckland, S. T., Burnham, K. P. and Augustin, N. H. (1997). Model selection: an integral part of inference. Biometrics 53, 603-618.

Ritz, C., Gerhard, D. and Hothorn, L. A. (2013). A unified framework for benchmark dose estimation applied to mixed models and model averaging. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research 5, 79-90.

EFSA Scientific Committee (2017). Update: use of the benchmark dose approach in risk assessment. EFSA Journal 15(1), 4658.

See also

bmd, bmdbayes, bmdefsa

Examples

fit <- function(model, family = "gaussian")
  drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = model, family = family,
         start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))
LL <- fit("loglogistic")
W1 <- fit("weibull1")
W2 <- fit("weibull2")
# AIC weights and the BMD of the averaged curve, without bootstrap
bmdma(LL = LL, W1 = W1, W2 = W2, bmr = 0.05, def = "relative", nsim = 0)
#> Model-averaged benchmark doses, relative deviation, averaged curves:
#> 
#>          model   family logLik df   AIC   weight    BMD
#> LL loglogistic gaussian -18.60  4 45.21 0.138258 0.9909
#> W1    weibull1 gaussian -22.22  4 52.44 0.003717 0.7538
#> W2    weibull2 gaussian -16.78  4 41.56 0.858025 1.3520
#> 
#>           BMD
#> 0.05:lf1 1.31
# \donttest{
# with a bootstrap BMDL
ma <- bmdma(LL = LL, W1 = W1, W2 = W2, bmr = 0.05, def = "relative", nsim = 100, seed = 1)
ma
#> Model-averaged benchmark doses, relative deviation, averaged curves:
#> 
#>          model   family logLik df   AIC   weight    BMD
#> LL loglogistic gaussian -18.60  4 45.21 0.138258 0.9909
#> W1    weibull1 gaussian -22.22  4 52.44 0.003717 0.7538
#> W2    weibull2 gaussian -16.78  4 41.56 0.858025 1.3520
#> 
#>           BMD   BMDL  BMDU
#> 0.05:lf1 1.31 0.8222 1.492
#> 
#> Bootstrap percentile intervals (100 samples), level 90%
confint(ma)
#>                5 %     95 %
#> 0.05:lf1 0.8221607 1.491713
# }
